data.long_meaning: Dhrishta (Seer) + Dyumna (Skilled or Intelligent). The name Dhrishtadyumna carries the meaning “Skilled Seer” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dhrishtadyumna usually hope their child will grow to embody skilled seer and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Dhrishtadyumna" holds significant importance in Hindu mythology. He was a great warrior from the Mahabharata war who was the son of Bhishma Pitamaha (Grandfather Bhishma) and Vidura, the royal preceptor of the Kuru kingdom. Dhrishtadyumna is known for his exceptional vision and intelligence, which earned him the name Dhrishta (Seer) and Dyumna (Skilled or Intelligent). As a prominent figure in this epic, his name resonates with the values of wisdom, bravery, and intelligence that are deeply rooted in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name "Dhrishtadyumna" signifies clear vision and deep understanding. The first part of the name, Dhrishta, means the one who can see the truth. It symbolizes the importance of having a clear understanding of the self and the world around us in our spiritual journey. The second part of the name, Dyumna, represents intelligence and knowledge. It underscores the significance of lifelong learning and the pursuit of knowledge in attaining spiritual growth. Thus, the name "Dhrishtadyumna" embodies the soul's quest for knowledge, clarity, and self-understanding, ultimately leading to enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dhrishtadyumna: Radiant and Unyielding Vision. The name embodies the power of clear, unwavering perception and the courage to stand firm against adversity.

historical_references.context: Dhrishtadyumna is the son of Bhishma Pitamaha and Vidura. He is one of the five Pandava brothers, and is the eldest among the Kshatriya brothers. Dhrishtadyumna leads the charge of the Pandava army against the Kaurava army on the fifteenth day of the Battle of Kurukshetra.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Mahabharata, Book 12, Chapter 74: The Slaying of Bhishma The name Dhrishtadyumna carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Dhrishtadyumna, as per Bhagavad Gita and Mahabharata, is the one who finally defeats Bhishma, the grandsire of the Kuru dynasty, after the great warrior lies on a bed of arrows for eighteen days. Dhrishtadyumna's success in killing Bhishma is significant because Bhishma was considered invincible in battle.

trends: Role in the battle of Kurukshetra
modern_usage.modern_context: Dhrishtadyumna is a significant character in Indian mythology, best known for his role in the epic Mahabharata during the battle of Kurukshetra. In literature, he is a popular subject for scholarly works and modern retellings of the Mahabharata. In television, Dhrishtadyumna has appeared in various adaptations and interpretations of the Mahabharata, including the popular Indian series 'Mahabharat'. In gaming, he has been featured as a playable character in games such as 'Mahabharata: Rise of the Kauravas'. Overall, Dhrishtadyumna continues to be a relevant and popular figure in contemporary Indian culture.
